target_domain.basis: Proposal S2.2 defines this review as a comparison against the framework in [7,8,10]; [9] is the same architecture line by the same group. T is the union of OpenAlex topics those four seeds carry at score >= topic_score_min. Using the framework's own topical fingerprint as the target avoids naming topics by hand. NOTE: seed_refs stays pre-registered at [7,8,9,10] and deliberately did NOT follow the v1.5.0 retag of [2] and [9] into framework_core. As measured, T is five broad Industrial & Manufacturing Engineering topics, none agent-specific, so p(s)/q(s) work as a dilution signal for ORDERING and cannot adjudicate agent-vs-DT. They no longer gate anything, so that limitation now costs ranking quality rather than recall.

precision.basis: p(s) over fewer than min_sample references is noise -- [11] Kusiak has 4 indexed references. Below the minimum, the weight falls back to the mean of same-role seeds that clear it, then to the global mean, and the basis field records the substitution. If nothing at all is measurable the weighting goes uniform at 1.0 rather than zero: 'could not measure' must not silently become 'counts for nothing'. Seeds with an empty OpenAlex reference list are coded no_references -- a data gap, not a precision finding.

forward_precision.basis: q(s), the forward mirror of p(s): the fraction of works CITING seed s that carry a topic in T. Backward references ride free on the seed record, but citing works do not, so q(s) is estimated from a deterministic random sample -- OpenAlex `sample=N&seed=S`, which returns the same works on every run with the same seed. This is a RANDOM sample, unlike a pagination-order cap, so it is a legitimate estimator rather than a hidden inclusion criterion. est_unique_citations is retained as a diagnostic; it was the volume term of the forward gate, removed in v1.6.0.

scoring.basis: score(c) = sum of precision(s) over every seed s linking to candidate c, in the direction each edge was followed, replacing the raw n_seed_links integer as the ranking term. A seed reaching a candidate both ways contributes once, at the higher weight. Downweighting is auditable where exclusion is not: a low-ranked paper is still in candidates.csv with its score and its seed links attached. Since v1.6.0 this is the ONLY thing p(s)/q(s) do.

policy.rationale: v2.0.0 REMOVES both hard gates and the min_discrimination_ratio diagnostic. This file now governs RANKING ONLY. The only retrieval policy is the expand_backward / expand_forward columns of seeds.csv; nothing computed at run time decides what is retrieved. The gates are gone because they never bit (the forward gate fired on zero seeds at the v1.5.0 measurement, the only high-volume seeds being the dt_survey six that seeds.csv already turns off by hand) and because the ratio they leaned on measured 1.05-1.3 against its own 1.3 floor -- T barely separates framework_core from dt_survey, so a gate that did not fire was abstaining rather than clearing. Thresholds here remain pre-registered: commit this file BEFORE the run it governs, so the sequence is verifiable from git history. Changing one after seeing results is a new policy_version and a new commit, not an edit.

seed_precision.note: p(s) and q(s) are measured from OpenAlex `topics`, itself a classifier with its own error rate; the raw counts are reported here so a reader can judge rather than taking the threshold as objective. q(s) additionally rests on a seeded random sample of citing works -- reproducible, but an estimate with sampling error of roughly 0.5/sqrt(n_sampled).

note: Retrieval, deduplication and counting performed deterministically. No language model contributed to this reference list. See proposal S3.3 and [26] on FM numerical reliability.

before.basis: rows OpenAlex supplied an abstract for

after.basis: after Semantic Scholar backfill by DOI

abstract_backfill.abstract_source_basis: Derived from the append-only call log, not from the CSV column and not from abstract presence: a rerun must not relabel rows S2 filled as openalex.
abstract_backfill.note: abstract_source=none rows are excluded from the calibration sample (a kappa mixing title-only and title+abstract decisions measures two tasks) and are forced to `uncertain` in production screening. unrecovered_transient_failures counts rows that a rerun with --refresh-errors could still fix; if it is non-zero the `none` count is an upper bound, not a finding.

calibration_sample.rng: python random.Random(rng_seed); strata sorted by paper_id, then random.sample() per stratum, then shuffle() of the 50
calibration_sample.pool_definition: eligible == True (eligibility.csv) AND abstract_source in openalex|semantic_scholar AND abstract non-empty
calibration_sample.excluded_no_abstract_basis: eligible rows only; ineligible rows are counted under excluded_ineligible

pool_exclusion_by_full_list_third.basis: Thirds are cut on the POOL, so these rates say how much that choice mattered. Equal rates mean cutting before or after the filters was the same decision; divergent rates mean pool exclusion is rank-correlated and the pool cut sits at a different paper than the full-list cut would.

calibration_sample.note: kappa computed on this sample is a kappa ON A STRATIFIED SAMPLE. It is not an estimate of kappa over the full ranked corpus, because the top third is deliberately oversampled 2:1 to put enough includes in the denominator for include-recall to mean anything. `stratum` is carried on every sample row so a later analysis can reweight. labels_TODO.csv omits stratum, rank and every seed-linkage column: a rater who can see how the pipeline ranked a paper is not an independent rater, and the resulting kappa would measure agreement with the ranking instead of agreement about the criteria.

fulltext_head.truncation: first N CHARACTERS of the extracted text; a character count, not a token estimate. No model is involved.
fulltext_head.cleaning: lines repeating on >=3 pages dropped as running headers/footers; bare page numbers dropped; affiliation lines dropped only in the first 40 lines and only when a line both names an institution and carries an email or an affiliation marker. Deliberately timid -- title-page matter may remain.
fulltext_head.elsevier_path: removed in v2.0.0 with the 2026-10-05 access rule; eligible 10.1016 rows are OA by definition and go through the OA path like any other
fulltext_head.scope: eligible rows (eligibility.py) lacking an abstract; ineligible rows are not targeted and not modified

before.basis: eligible rows with abstract_source=none at the start of this run

after.basis: eligible rows still with no abstract and no full-text head

fulltext_head.note: A full-text head is NOT an abstract: it is the opening of the paper, truncated by character count, and it is stored in its own column so the screening prompt can label it as such. Because it is a different input distribution, these rows are calibrated on their own 20-paper sample rather than mixed into the 50-paper abstract sample. Eligible rows still at abstract_source=none are screened on title alone and forced to `uncertain`; ineligible rows are not screened at all.

calibration_sample_fulltext.rng: python random.Random(rng_seed); pool sorted by paper_id, then random.sample(), then shuffle()
calibration_sample_fulltext.census_note: The draw took the ENTIRE eligible pool, so no sampling occurred and rng_seed selected nothing -- these 20 are every full-text-head row that exists, not a sample of them. Metrics computed here describe this set exactly and generalise to nothing wider. The pool is small because the Elsevier source was skipped for want of an API key; when it runs, the pool grows by up to 217 and this draw should be redone as an actual sample.

thresholds.basis: same floors as the abstract sample; the input differs, the bar does not

calibration_sample_fulltext.note: Scored SEPARATELY from the 50-paper abstract sample and never pooled with it: a truncated full-text head is a different input distribution, and one kappa over both would describe neither. The two samples cannot overlap by construction, since a row carries either an abstract or a head. Caveat on size: 20 is a small denominator for include-recall, and unlike the 50-paper draw this one is unstratified, so if includes are rare in the pool the recall estimate will be noisy. eligible_pool is recorded so that can be judged rather than assumed.

eligibility.decided_by: advisor meeting 2026-10-05: candidates restricted to accessible papers
rules_in_order: OpenAlex open_access.is_oa false AND no Unpaywall OA location (oa_locations empty, or DOI unknown to Unpaywall) -> ineligible, no_oa. No DOI: OpenAlex is_oa alone.
eligibility.rule_history: v1 (commit 1a41053) also had rule 1: DOI prefix 10.1016 -> ineligible `elsevier`, even when OA. Removed 2026-10-05 in v2.0.0. v1 decisions and provenance: corpus/archive/2026-10-05_eligibility_v1/. Effect of the removal: see doi_10_1016_rows.

inputs.openalex: GET /works?filter=openalex:<ids>&select=id,doi,open_access, 50 IDs per request; IDs missing from the batch retried singly via /works/<id> (follows merges)
inputs.unpaywall: GET /v2/<doi>; queried for every row with a DOI where OpenAlex is_oa is false or the OpenAlex record is missing (404)

manual_overrides.reason: What it is: Elharrouss, Akbari, Almaadeed and Al-Maadeed (2022), 'Backbones-Review: Feature Extraction Networks for Deep Learning and Deep Reinforcement Learning Approaches', an arXiv preprint (arXiv:2206.08016, DOI 10.48550/arxiv.2206.08016) surveying deep-learning feature-extraction backbones. Why the rules could not decide it: rule 1 does not apply (not a 10.1016 DOI). Rule 2 needs OpenAlex open_access.is_oa, but OpenAlex deleted the work after the 2026-09-28 build (GET /works/W4283074224 returns 404; filter doi:10.48550/arxiv.2206.08016 returns 0 results). The Unpaywall fallback cannot answer either: Unpaywall indexes Crossref DOIs and returns 404 for this DataCite (arXiv) DOI. With neither input, rules 1-3 cannot decide it. Why eligible: the 2026-09-28 build recorded oa_pdf_url=https://arxiv.org/pdf/2206.08016 from OpenAlex, and arXiv full texts are openly accessible, so the paper meets the intent of the access rule. Eligibility only puts it in scope for screening; it makes no topical judgment.

eligibility.manual_overrides_note: Human judgments, not rule outputs: rows that neither OpenAlex nor Unpaywall could answer for. Applied only where the rules could not decide. Source: corpus/eligibility_overrides.csv
eligibility.candidates_key_basis: SHA-256 of ordered (openalex_id, lowercased doi) pairs; the staleness check
eligibility.rank_stratum_definition: position in the FULL ranked candidates.csv (corpus_build.py rank order); top_third = ranks 1..n//3, bottom_two_thirds = the rest. Same cut as draw_calibration_sample.py but on the full list, since eligibility is decided before any filtering.

top_excluded_venues.venue: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering

eligibility.top_excluded_venues_basis: top 15 venues by count of ineligible rows (either reason), ties broken alphabetically; blank venue reported as '(no venue)'. 291 distinct venues have at least one excluded row.

doi_10_1016_rows.note: Rule 1 (10.1016 -> ineligible regardless of OA) was removed in v2.0.0; these rows are decided by the OA rule alone. Every one of them was ineligible under v1 (corpus/archive/2026-10-05_eligibility_v1/), so `eligible` here is exactly the number of rows the removal brought into scope.

eligibility.note: Eligibility is a scope decision, not a screening decision. Ineligible rows keep their row in eligibility.csv, are never sent to a screening model, and are never forced to `uncertain`: they are out of scope, not undecided. Counts here are the 'excluded at eligibility' stage; 'excluded at screening' is reported separately by benchmark.py.
